nominal_scale.kind: nominal art-direction choice, not a newly measured fossil dimension; display scaling separately labeled

budget_intent.policy: 14k triangles and 1,000,000 bytes are ceilings, not targets. Usually aim about 100–500 KB; below this range is fine. Spend more triangles only for visible silhouette/proportion/connection benefit. Do not pad counts or enlarge textures for apparent refinement. Preserve quality if a justified asset exceeds the usual range within the hard caps.

start_gate: Next round is planning only; parent explicit exclusive assignment needed. For already assigned workers, latest state and explicit parent dispatch override stale empty claims or initial queue snapshots.
concurrency: Parent-coordinated shared host pool; default one worker x two Blender threads, no per-batch full-host allocation.

design.observed: Thick sediment block containing one circular opening with unornamented continuously tapering negative walls, deep small rounded bottom. Side diagnostic depicts narrow rounded termination; top appears almost cylindrical near mouth and has dark center. Hero opening visually larger relative to block than requested.
design.resolve: Freeze opening diameter .084 m in .24 x .20 x .14 m sediment; cavity depth .112 m and small rounded basal termination. Preserve negative cavity; no almond outline. Published KGS genus description gives rounded base; specific C. conicus may have small planar apical disc. Therefore pointed-bottom means strongly converging narrow base, not unsupported mathematically sharp point. Supplement exact-GLB gray top and oblique with a labelled diagnostic half-section; main delivered GLB remains intact.
design.masses: One fully volumetric closed sediment mesh with real top annulus and inward-facing cone wall, continuous substrate below cavity, and quiet layered outer walls. Small rounded basal cap is part of mesh; no positive cone. Diagnostic bisect is explanatory and separately recorded.
